messages:
From: Claire Park <claire@fastmedhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: exploring Private deployment options for pilot (pricing questions)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team is excited. Before we get legal involved we need a clearer commercial structure for the proposed private deployment (VPC + on-prem fallbacks). A few open questions from procurement and our CTO: 

- Can you provide a proposal that mixes a small committed pilot (3 months) with optional on-prem node licensing if we exceed the pilot usage? We want a hedged model rather than a single long commitment.
- How would Redwood amortize the platform fee for a short pilot? Any flexibility on spreading/platform credits?
- We need SRE retainer tiers; our ops team will want a guaranteed response window and an option to add on-call hours if we scale.
- Legal will likely ask for a simple IP/data carveout — can you point to typical language or evidence (audit logs, KMS) we can attach?

I've attached a rough pilot usage spreadsheet. Can you send a concise counterproposal with 2–3 packaging options (pilot-credit, amortized platform fee, retainer tiers) and estimated ARR impact so our CFO can preview?

Claire
Procurement Lead, FastMed Health
Attachment: Pilot_Usage_Estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet, 32KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire@fastmedhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: exploring Private deployment options for pilot (pricing questions)

Claire — thanks for the clear list. Below are three practical packaging options that match Redwood patterns and the use-case you described. I kept the summary short so you can share with CFO and CTO; happy to jump on a 30m call.

Option A — Pilot-first (lowest upfront)
- 3-month pilot commit: 50k USD prepay credits (applies to metered usage and infra consumption).
- Platform fee: waived for pilot months; platform fee (monthly) starts after pilot or converts to 60% prepay credit applied to month 4 if customer converts.
- SRE retainer: optional add-on, monthly SOC: 8x5 response, 1 hour on-call included. Additional on-call billed at a reduced hourly rate.
- Escrow / security: provide SOC2 report + KMS integration checklist; limited audit evidence pack included.

Option B — Amortized commitment (balanced)
- 12-month minimum with 6 months invoiced upfront, remaining 6 months amortized quarterly.
- Platform fee: amortized across 12 months; we can offer a 20% credit if you commit to a 12-month volume baseline.
- SRE retainer: Tier 1 (8x5), Tier 2 (24x7 on-call) — discounted if bundled for 12 months.

Option C — On-prem licensing hedge (conversion path)
- Pilot run under hosted/dedicated VPC credits for 3 months, with a pre-agreed conversion formula to on-prem perpetual license + 12-month SRE retainer. Conversion credit: 30–50% of pilot credits applied to license price depending on commit size.
- Platform fee: one-time onboarding fee (discountable against license) + optional annual platform maintenance.

Next steps I suggest: we share a short SOW (I attached draft v3) that maps to Option A and Option C — that gives legal something concrete to redline. If this looks aligned, I’ll loop in Irene (commercial ops) for the amortization/legal language and Marissa for onboarding/SRE scoping.

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: FastMed_SOW_draft_v3.pdf (SOW draft, 48KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: FW: Hybrid licensing hedge proposal & SRE retainer bands for FastMed pilot — need commercial signoff

Irene/Marissa — forwarding Claire's ask and my counterproposal. Quick background: FastMed is a regional healthcare SaaS buyer; pilot looks constrained (3 months) but with clear upside to convert to on-prem if they hit throughput thresholds. Legal will request audit evidence and typical data carveouts.

Please review and advise on the following by EOD tomorrow: 
1) Amortization approach for Option B — I proposed 12-month amortization with 6 months upfront. Would finance accept 18 months amortization at reduced platform fee (helps their runway)?
2) Conversion credit band for Option C — I've suggested 30–50% pilot-credit-to-license credit. Is 30% floor acceptable? Any minimum license SKU constraints?
3) SRE retainer language — Marissa, can you draft two bullets we can include in SOW: (a) Tier 1: 8x5, 4hr P1 response, standard on-call; (b) Tier 2: 24x7, 1hr P1 response + optional escalated on-call hours pack. Pricing placeholders are fine.

I want the words we put in the SOW to be legible to legal — Irene, can you add a short amortization clause and a DocuSign-ready invoice schedule after you confirm amortization term?

Thanks — I kept Claire on to reduce back-and-forth.

— Logan
(On behalf of Redwood Commercial Ops)

Logan — appreciate the clear options and quick follow. FastMed prefers Option C (Pilot -> conversion hedge) with the following asks before legal signs: 

- Confirm conversion credit floor at 35% (we can accept up to 45% depending on committed baseline).
- Platform onboarding fee to be credited back if we convert within 90 days.
- SRE Tier 2 sample SLA language (1hr P1) and a priced optional 100-hour on-call block.
- A short evidence pack for legal: SOC2 + KMS integration checklist and sample audit log export (redacted).

If you can update the SOW to reflect: 35% conversion floor, onboarding credit if converted within 90 days, and include the SRE bullets, we can route to our legal team today. If you send the DocuSign link for the pilot SOW with the changes I’ll route and expedite.

Claire
